title: Inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement

card.complaint: Central chest pain and sweating for 45 minutes

triage.note: Brought in by family. Crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm for 45 minutes, with sweating and nausea. Known diabetic and smoker.

appearance.text: Pain easing, less sweaty, talking comfortably.
Grey and sweaty, clutching his chest. Pain 8/10, nauseated.
Pale, cold and clammy, restless. Pain 10/10.

history.a: It started 45 minutes ago climbing the stairs. Like an elephant sitting on my chest. It goes into my jaw and left arm.

history.q: How bad is it, out of 10?
history.a: Nine out of ten. The worst pain of my life.
I’m sweating buckets and I feel sick. A little breathless.

history.q: Have you had anything like this before?
history.a: For a few weeks I’ve had tightness walking uphill that went away with rest. Never this bad.
Diabetes for 10 years and high blood pressure. The doctor said my cholesterol is high.
Metformin and amlodipine. I stopped the statin because it gave me aches.

history.q: Any sildenafil or tadalafil in the last 48 hours?
Any bleeding problems, recent surgery, stroke or ulcer?
Any heart disease in the family?
history.a: My father died of a heart attack at 60.

exam.label: General
exam.text: Grey, sweaty, anxious, in obvious pain.

exam.label: Cardiovascular
exam.text: Pulse 54, regular, low volume. JVP raised to 6 cm. Heart sounds normal, no murmurs. Radial pulses equal.

exam.label: Peripheries
exam.text: Cool peripheries, capillary refill 3 s. No calf swelling.

investigations.label: 12-lead ECG
investigations.text: Sinus bradycardia 54/min. ST elevation 3 mm in II, III and aVF (III > II). Reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. ST elevation in V1. Consider right-sided leads.

investigations.label: Right-sided ECG (V4R)
investigations.text: 1.5 mm ST elevation in V4R: right ventricular involvement.

investigations.label: Focused echo (POCUS)
investigations.text: Inferior wall hypokinesia. Dilated, hypokinetic RV. No pericardial effusion. LV function mildly reduced.

investigations.label: FBC, U&E, coagulation
investigations.text: Hb 13.8 g/dL, platelets 240 ×10⁹/L, creatinine 98 µmol/L (1.1 mg/dL), K⁺ 4.2 mmol/L, INR 1.0.

investigations.label: Chest X-ray (portable)
investigations.text: Normal heart size and mediastinum. Clear lungs.

interventions.label: Apply defibrillator pads
interventions.say: Nurse: “Pads on, defibrillator in monitor mode.”

interventions.label: GTN 400 micrograms sublingual

harm.why: Nitrates are contraindicated with systolic BP < 90 mmHg, suspected right ventricular infarction (preload-dependent) and PDE-5 inhibitor use in the previous 24–48 h. This patient had all three.

interventions.say: Nurse: “GTN given… his pressure is dropping.”

interventions.label: Morphine 2.5 mg IV, titrated
interventions.feedback: Opioids relieve pain but can worsen hypotension and delay absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors. Titrate small doses.

interventions.label: Atropine 500 micrograms IV
interventions.feedback: Reasonable for symptomatic bradycardia with hypotension in inferior MI. Here the hypotension is mainly RV failure, so fluids help more.

interventions.label: High-flow oxygen
interventions.feedback: Routine oxygen is not recommended in acute coronary syndromes when SpO₂ is ≥ 90%.

harm.why: Fibrinolysis is for when primary PCI cannot be delivered within 120 minutes of diagnosis. In a PCI-capable centre it adds bleeding risk without benefit over primary PCI.

interventions.label: Activate cath lab
interventions.say: Cardiology: “Cath lab activated. Table ready in 20 minutes.”

diagnoses.label: Inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement

dispositions.label: Cath lab for primary PCI, then CCU
Admit to CCU for medical management; angiography tomorrow
Thrombolyse in the ED, then transfer to a PCI centre
Admit to a general ward for serial troponins

critical.label: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes
critical.why: STEMI is diagnosed on the ECG. Record it within 10 minutes of first medical contact.

critical.label: Cath lab activated for primary PCI
critical.why: Primary PCI is the preferred reperfusion strategy when it can be delivered within 120 minutes of diagnosis.

critical.label: Monitoring attached
critical.why: Risk of VF and brady-arrhythmia is highest in the first hours.

recommended.label: Right-sided ECG to look for RV infarction

penalties.why: Oxygen was given with SpO₂ ≥ 92%. Routine oxygen does not help in ACS unless SpO₂ is < 90%.
Two different P2Y12 inhibitors were loaded. Give one.
Two different P2Y12 inhibitors were loaded. Give one.

teaching: Record and read a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact. STEMI is an ECG diagnosis: do not wait for troponin.
In inferior STEMI, record right-sided leads (V4R). RV involvement is common; the clue is hypotension with a raised JVP and clear lungs.
RV infarction is preload-dependent: avoid nitrates and diuretics and give cautious fluid boluses.
Nitrates are contraindicated with SBP < 90 mmHg, RV infarction, and sildenafil in the past 24 h or tadalafil in the past 48 h.
Aspirin loading plus a P2Y12 inhibitor; anticoagulation at the time of PCI.
Primary PCI if it can be delivered within 120 minutes of diagnosis. Otherwise give fibrinolysis within 10 minutes of diagnosis and transfer.
Oxygen only if SpO₂ < 90%. Put pads on early: VF risk is highest in the first hours.
references: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes.
Resuscitation Council UK. Adult advanced life support guidelines (2021).
